short_title: Pallotto, nuncio at Vienna, cipher dispatches 1628 (BAV Barb.lat.6956) with Rome's decifrati (Barb.lat.6960)
writer: Giovanni Battista Pallotto, nuncio at the imperial court
recipient: Cardinal Francesco Barberini, Secretariat of State (DECODE lists receiver 'emperor' for R315, which the page header contradicts)
matters: Urban VIII's nuncio at Vienna in the years of the Edict of Restitution and the Mantuan war; but the clear text of his dispatches is printed (Kiewning), so unread text would add little beyond the key itself
matters_src: PRIMARY: https://de-crypt.org/decrypt-web/RecordsView/315 and /RecordsView/285 (DECODE R285-R318, Barb.lat.6956 and 6960, Non-decrypted); PRIMARY: http://digi.vatlib.it/view/MSS_Barb.lat.6960/0081 header 'Di Vienna da Mons. Pallotto ... Decifrata li 6 di settembre'; SCHOLARLY: Kiewning (ed.), Nuntiatur des Pallotto 1628-1630, NBD IV 1-2 (Berlin 1895-97), cited at https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/qufiab-2018-0004/html
not_taken: not in catalogue (grep Pallott/Barb.lat 6956/6960: none); not in taken-2026-11-19.tsv; no profile names Pallotto, R285-R318 or Barb.lat 6956; key: none found. Clear text printed by Kiewning from the decifrati (not opened: whether every cipher passage is printed). Not checked: whether Lasry/Megyesi 2020 papal-cipher work used these volumes
searches: DECODE RecordsList search 'nunzio'; web: Kiewning Pallotto Nuntiaturberichte Chiffre; web: BAV cifra decifrazione interlineare nunzio
pair: yes in principle: cipher in Barb.lat.6956, Rome's clear decifrati in Barb.lat.6960 (e.g. 6960/0081), and Kiewning's print; the pairing of a given cipher letter to its decifrato not checked
pair_signs: not checked (one full cipher page 6956/0064 is ~30 lines x ~90 digits = ~2,700 digits, by eye)
neighbour_keys: not checked; papal keys of the 1620s survive in AAV Segr. Stato Cifre (not online); Meister 1906 ends at 1600
second_passage: yes: Barb.lat.6956 holds many cipher dispatches (contact sheet: canvases 64, 73, 154, 163 dense digit blocks)
design: continuous digit strings, no separators, papal homophonic/nomenclator style (from 6956/0064)
notes: Bitonal microfilm at ~1100 px per page breaks digits into fragments; 8 px is under the 11 px of no. 1336. A colour rescan by BAV would breach it.
